thread:
michael: heads up — just finished the v4.2 rollout to prod (bundle: w-2026-04-03). getting a stream of client complaints and we have ~3% of /generate responses containing tokenization garbage (weird unicode escapes, repeated <unk>, truncated json outputs).

deploy-bot: Deploy started: v4.2 -> prod on cluster-east (rollout id r-8372). Canary target: 2% traffic.

oncall-jay: paging oncall — I'm on it. can you drop the rollout id and sample request IDs?

michael: sample reqs: rQ: 8e12f3, 8e12f4, 8e12f9. error pattern: tokenizer errors in the logs like `TokenizerError: vocab index out-of-range` and many outputs start with `\uFFFD` characters.

ben: pulling logs now. see spike at 12:14: server: inference-03 shows tokenizer init warnings: `vocab.len=50257 expected=50258` on model load.

sara: who validated the weight bundle mapping in CI? I can check the release manifest. this sounds like a misaligned vocab / weights pairing.

michael: release manifest shows model:v4.2 + tokenizer:v4.1 in the bundle. CI should have rejected that. it looks like manifest tag resolution fell back to latest-tokenizer which was v4.1 and not v4.2.

lisa: oh that explains it — the tokenizer was not pinned in the deploy graph. I'm guessing the new weights expect a different tokenizer length.

oncall-jay: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip `deploy.rollout` feature flag to abort further traffic to v4.2, 2) rollback to v4.1 weightset globally, 3) hotpatch tokens via tokenizer reload on the affected nodes. Which is fastest?

ben: fastest is flip the rollout flag — that routes new requests back to v4.1. rollback is heavier but safer if flag flip fails.

sara: I'm going to flip the rollout flag. @oncall-jay do we have an automated rollback if the flag flip doesn't reduce error rate in 2 mins?

oncall-jay: INCIDENT-BOT: page to oncall triggered for incident "misbound weights causing tokenizer drift" — priority P1.

incident-bot: oncall acknowledged. executing playbook step 1 (isolate rollout).

sara: flipping flag now: `POST /admin/flags/deploy.rollout?r=r-8372&state=abort`

support-bot: sent customer notice draft to #support for review: "We detected a degraded model rollout impacting generated responses. Rolling back to previous model version while we investigate. Apologies for the disruption."

ben: metrics — error rate on /generate dropped to 1.4% within 45s after flag flip, still above baseline 0.1%. appears some traffic still hitting v4.2 (in-flight requests or sticky sessions).

michael: can we kill active v4.2 instances? there are ~30 pods on cluster-east.

oncall-jay: I can drain pods but want to avoid dropping customer in-flight reqs. option: force label update on router to stop routing new sessions and then drain. running: `kubectl label svc/router-east release-allow=false`

ben: routers updated. new connections go to v4.1. still seeing retries from long-lived websocket sessions.

sara: I'll start a rollback job to move traffic fully back to w-2026-03-28 (v4.1) — `deployctl rollback --to w-2026-03-28 --strategy=immediate`

lisa: I'm also running a quick validation script against the candidate tokenizer for v4.2 to confirm mismatch: `python tools/validate_tokenizer.py --weights w-2026-04-03 --tokenizer t-4.2` -> failing with `vocab mismatch: 50257 != 50258`.

michael: root cause summary (prelim): deploy graph resolution allowed tokenizer v4.1 to pair with weights v4.2 due to missing explicit pin; weights expect a tokenizer with vocab size +1, causing token index OOB and garbled outputs.

ben: rollback job completed at +8m. traffic back to v4.1. error rate now at baseline 0.12%. can we mark incident as mitigated and begin postmortem?

oncall-jay: marking as mitigated. executing post-incident checklist: set incident status -> mitigated, create pager notes, notify stakeholders.

support-bot: support message sent to affected customers with ETA for full postmortem.

sara: immediate next steps: - pin tokenizer in release manifest and fail deploy if tokenizer and weights vocab lengths differ; - add a pre-rollout check that validates tokenizer-vocab vs weight-expected-vocab; - add an alert for tokenizer.init warnings (vocab mismatch).

lisa: I'll open PR for manifest pin enforcement now and add CI test. link will be in the postmortem.

michael: customers impacted: low volume but visible degradation to several business-critical customers using chat endpoints. ops estimates 7 customer incidents; support triage ongoing.

oncall-jay: assigning postmortem owner: @sara. timeline: draft within 48h, include impacted request IDs and mitigation steps.

incident-bot: incident closed for oncall rotation, leaving thread for postmortem comments. :white_check_mark:

michael: thanks everyone — please drop any logs/samples into the postmortem doc (link will be pinned). follow-up: consider automatic rollback when tokenizer mismatch is detected during canary.

ben: adding a short retention note: save the tokenizer and weight artifact bundles (w-2026-04-03 + t-4.1) to the incident artifacts bucket for debugging.

sara: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/pin-tokenizer-in-manifest/pull/124 — includes CI check and an e2e.

lisa: I'll schedule a quick 30m blameless runbook sync to update the deploy graph docs and submit changes to the release automation.

support-bot: ticket sent to customers who reported issues; CS will follow up if they need more detail.

michael: closing thread for live mitigation. leaving postmortem updates here when available. :thumbsup:
